Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sun, Nov 22 7:58am to 5:59pm; Mon, Nov 23 7:59am to 5:58pm; Tue, Nov 24 8am to 5:57pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sun, Nov 22 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Porteau is back in play. Pam Rocks has read N 21 to 25 gusting 30 since 6am, about 6 above the page, and the English Bay buoy N 21. Yesterday the beach took until about 12:30 to fill in from the same setup, so no rush: if Pam Rocks still reads N 22+ at 10:30am, go for noon to about 2pm. The tide floods to 14.9ft at 3:30pm, so the swell may soften late.

Backup: Boundary Bay in the SE from 2:30pm to last light, about 5:50pm. Sand Heads has eased to E 11, so skip the morning. Jericho beach is calm.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 PM PCT 22 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Monday. Wind northerly outflow 20 knots increasing to northerly outflow 25 late this evening then diminishing to northerly outflow 15 early Monday afternoon. Wind increasing to northerly outflow 25 Monday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 PM PCT 22 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Monday. Wind east 15 knots veering to southeast 20 early this evening then backing to east 25 near midnight. Wind east 25 Monday. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
